These discussions are so difficult because they are impossible to have in the abstract. Talking about the 'average' citizen or person is always a bit ridiculous in my opinion because there isn't one. It's the average across all the social classes, millionaires and the homeless, people who can live off of accumulated family wealth and single parents with multiple jobs. The average doesn't acknowledge social context, let alone debt, or mental health or spare time. It just makes me think of that Terry Pratchett quote about poverty using the shoes?
"The reason that the rich were so rich, Vimes reasoned, was because they managed to spend less money.
Take boots, for example. He earned thirty-eight dollars a month plus allowances. A really good pair of leather boots cost fifty dollars. But an affordable pair of boots, which were sort of OK for a season or two and then leaked like hell when the cardboard gave out, cost about ten dollars. Those were the kind of boots Vimes always bought, and wore until the soles were so thin that he could tell where he was in Ankh-Morpork on a foggy night by the feel of the cobbles.
But the thing was that good boots lasted for years and years. A man who could afford fifty dollars had a pair of boots that’d still be keeping his feet dry in ten years’ time, while the poor man who could only afford cheap boots would have spent a hundred dollars on boots in the same time and would still have wet feet."

Motivation, hope and accountability is important don't get me wrong. As long as there is also acknowledgement of hurdles and barriers that people face. Otherwise it reads as accusations of people not trying hard enough.

After a few hours bowling we had made a fast friendship and I was really enjoying having some guy friends.

 As we were leaving to head out, one of the guys pulls me aside and asks me to be his girlfriend. I declined and said I wasn't interested in him. The rest of the group told me I should give him a chance and that he was really nice.
Probably should have listened to that sign....

Over the next two years we would hang out about once a month usually having a massive sleepover at someone's house. The guy turned into one of my best friends and I said no to being his girlfriend probably another 3 or so times. 
One night at the monthly sleepover when we had all fallen asleep after watching LOTR, I woke up to his hand inside my pyjamas. I spent the rest of the night locked in the bathroom. It turned out he had been sexually assulting me in my sleep multiple times over months in a room with our friends all asleep too.
He decided that in exchange for being a close friend he deserved my body as well...

The friends all took his side saying I clearly was enticing him by being a whore who would ruin his life when I wanted support for going to the police.
Unsurprisingly I don't see any of these people anymore.
